A Constraint Only Works When an Unbriefed Viewer Sees the Difference It Makes

Your current Screening Room draft collapses because it stacks six unexplained project names at the top, buries the films beneath seventeen unfilmed workshops, blurs real 20th-century classics with newly built one-minute proof cuts, and strips out the founders' actual words. Fixing it requires stating one sharp thesis, separating four levels of reality, and naming the exact difference that separates every workshop and film (audited November 2026).

9 / 25

New proof films in the Screening Room that pass a blind viewer check without prior explanation of the rule.

17

Executable Ouxpo workshop specs in the Prompt Library, not yet filmed, all testing one five-prop station scene.

61 / 99

Completed mixed-media pages of the in-house 99 Ways station book; the leaf-through film waits for page 99.

2 to 19

Credited open-license archival clips or handmade assets per proof film. Zero pirated classics, zero AI stock slop.

Why the Current Draft Fails and What the Actual Thesis Is

Right now, a visitor landing on paeleo/scion/oulipo/screening/ hits eleven title lines (CRASH LAB, PAELEO, SCION, Oulipo prompts, Screening Room, Ouxpo), then reads a complaint about melting AI pixels, then scrolls past seventeen workshop blurbs that have no films on the page, and finally meets cards like Alain Resnais and Raymond Queneau · 1958 · Le Chant du styrène · 0:38 without knowing whether they are clicking a 1958 French film clip or an AI remake.

The project does not exist to complain about commercial AI video. Its thesis joins Jacques Roubaud's Oulipo principle with Gregory Bateson's cybernetic definition of information and PAELEO's PEO method: a formal rule is an experimental instrument. Hold the raw incident or footage fixed, apply one strict structural rule, and ask a blind viewer who was never told the rule what changed on screen. If the rule produces a perceptible shift in cause, suspicion, rhythm, or meaning, the film passes. If the rule stays trapped inside the prompt while the screen looks generic, the film fails.

"A text written according to a constraint describes the constraint." (Jacques Roubaud) · "The unit of information is a difference, which makes a difference." (Gregory Bateson, 1972)

Drop-In Replacement Intro for the Top of the Screening Room

Cut the eleven-line header stack and move the seventeen unfilmed workshops below the films (or keep them in the Prompt Library). Put the thesis, what is real, and the blind test right above the player grid.

Screening Room · 25 Proof Films After Oulipo, Oucipo, and Oubapo

The thesis: In 1960, Raymond Queneau and François Le Lionnais founded the Oulipo to prove that strict formal rules unlock sharper art than unguided habit, calling themselves "rats who must build the labyrinth from which they propose to escape." Jacques Roubaud added the group's hardest test: a work built under a constraint must make that constraint legible to its audience. This room applies Roubaud's test to autonomous AI filmmaking.

What you are watching (what is real): None of the 25 films below is a clip of the historical movie, comic, or novel named on its slate. Each is a new 22-to-75-second proof film built by a six-role SCION agent crew executing the formal rule of that historical work. Every frame and sound is foraged or handmade, never faked: either open-license archival material (2 to 19 credited public-domain or Creative Commons sources per film) or purpose-built paper puppets, ink drawings, and folded comic pages.

Why failures stay up: After the crew renders a cut and a rights reviewer clears every license, blind readers watch cold without seeing the prompt. If an unbriefed viewer cannot see the rule make a difference on screen, the independent critic fails the cut. Today 9 pass, 6 miss on one narrow point, 8 fail (including La Machine à tuer le temps and La Belle Hortense), and 2 are earlier pre-crew builds.

What Is Real Here: Separating Four Objects Currently Mixed Together

Visitors lose their footing when historical citations, prompt code, new films, and unfinished books share the same visual weight. Every item across PAELEO, SCION / OULIPO, and the Screening Room belongs to one of four distinct realities.

1. Historical Canon (1926 to 2023)

Real works by Duchamp, Queneau, Resnais, Perec, Calvino, Roubaud, Lécroart, Madden, Orchard, and Martino, plus unfilmed archival dossiers like Oucipo's 42-photo Machine à tuer le temps (Drouot lot 175). They supply the rule, never pirated footage.

2. 25 Proof Films (Live MP4s)

Real 22-to-75-second films built by SCION crews for Cinema (10), Comics (7, five with printable comic sheets via The page), Variations & Literature (5), and Animation (3), audited publicly by a blind critic.

3. 17 Workshop Specs (No Film Yet)

Real .poml and .md system instructions in the Prompt Library testing one five-prop railway-station incident across seventeen Ouxpo crafts. They are runnable assignments, not completed films.

4. 99 Ways Book (61 / 99 Built)

Sixty-one real mixed-media pages (01 · Template through 62 · Prisoner's text, with #59 and #63 to #99 still open) retelling that station incident in-house. Its leaf-through film does not exist yet.

Seven Core Names: Exact Definition, Verbatim Quote, and What Separates Each

On bolas/paeleo/, the institutional and technical terms nest cleanly like crates, whereas on the Screening Room draft they currently blur into synonyms. Table 1 pairs each name's exact expansion and verbatim source quote with the boundary that distinguishes it from every neighbor.

Name & Expansion Strict Definition Verbatim Primary Quote The Difference That Makes the Difference
AEL & CRASH LAB
Augmented Environments Lab		 The physical Georgia Tech research laboratory and historical lineage investigating situated media worlds. "Where situated worlds are investigated and made. The laboratory and its historical lineage." (PAELEO) Names the place and institutional lineage, not the authoring language (PAELEO), method (PEO), or agent crew (SCION).
PAELEO
Promptable Augmented Environments Lab / Language for Ekphrastic Operations		 Both the studio practice and the formal language where world descriptions are written, executed, and audited; deliberately echoes paleo (excavating buried media futures). "From describing worlds to operating within them." · "The language and working environment in which descriptions can be authored, executed, contested and evaluated." (PAELEO) Replaces passive pixel streams with executable world state so changing one rule or motive leaves the rest of the world intact.
PEO
Prompt · Ekphrasis · Operation		 The three-step authoring grammar and dissertation method (Operative Ekphrasis) turning verbal constraint into testable physical consequence. "How descriptions become consequential actions. Its object is not simply a prompt, but a situated operation with observable consequences." (PAELEO) Separates a raw text prompt from an observable state transition; unlike loose prompt engineering, every description must cash out in measurable action.
SCION
System-Instruction Compiler & Operator Network		 Both the .poml/.md specification compiler and the six-role agent crew (director, builders, editor, blind readers, critic, rights reviewer) that runs it. "Convert the supplied prompt, workflow, tool, research corpus, or creative brief into a complete system instruction another capable agent can use." (SCION #s26) Splits making from judging: the builder swarm never grades its own work, and the blind reader never sees the prompt.
Oulipo
Ouvroir de littérature potentielle (1960)		 Paris research workshop founded by François Le Lionnais and Raymond Queneau to excavate old literary constraints (anoulipism) and invent mathematical new ones (synthoulipism). "Oulipians: rats who must build the labyrinth from which they propose to escape." · "The only literature is voluntary literature." (Lescure / Queneau, 1961) Fashions reusable potential structures rather than one-off inspired texts, opposing both Surrealist chance and statistical averaging.
Ouxpo
Ouvroir d'X Potentiels (1973 onward)		 Umbrella coordinated inside the Collège de 'Pataphysique extending Oulipian constraint research to any discipline X (crime, cinema, painting, comics, theatre, cooking, code). "Each ouvroir is dedicated to some field 'X'. It analyses the pre-existing constraints, and investigates new forms of potential creations within the field." (Ouxpo) Moves constraint out of words alone into space, frame counts, ink folds, soundtracks, floor plans, and agendas.
ALAMO & Anticombinatorics
Paul Braffort, Jacques Roubaud & Italo Calvino (1973 to 1981)		 The computational wing of Oulipo using software either to fill typed grammatical molds or to filter trillions of narrative permutations down to valid survivors. "among a large number of possibilities, the computer selects those few realizations compatible with certain constraints." (Calvino, 1981) Uses computation as a sieve that eliminates invalid worlds rather than a generator that spews unconstrained text.

The 17 Workshops: Exact Thesis and the Boundary Between Neighbors

In the Prompt Library, all seventeen non-film workshops operate on the exact same five-element railway-station incident (a visitor, a sealed envelope, a bell, a brass key left on a bench, a closed service door). Holding the incident constant exposes the exact operational difference between every workshop and its closest cousin, anchored below in the verbatim creative theses from your SCION cards.

Workshop & Craft Definition & SCION Creative Thesis The Difference That Makes the Difference
Oulipo
Literature (1960)		 6 line-slots × 3 interchangeable alternatives ($3^6 = 729$ assemblies) filtered by a letter ban. "Write one event as a family of texts... Use the missing letter to discover which facts are hardest to name." vs. ALAMO: Oulipo authors full interchangeable sentences and bans a letter to force paraphrase; ALAMO splits one text's syntax from another text's vocabulary.
ALAMO
Computational prose (1981)		 Fixed syntactic mold filled strictly from an external donor lexicon. "Make the mold and the dictionary independently inspectable so a reader can tell which text supplies the sentence shape and which supplies its verbal material." vs. Oulipo & Ou'inpo: Separates grammar from lexicon as two auditable inputs rather than permuting whole lines or executing computer code.
Ou'inpo
Software code (1997)		 Executable program whose first characters per line spell a vertical acrostic. vs. Outypopo: Ou'inpo must compile and compute a live software result; Outypopo never executes code and never alters a single word of source prose.
Outypopo
Typography (2023)		 Verbatim prose re-broken across line endings so the left or right margin spells an acrostic. vs. Ou'inpo & Ougrapo: Wording stays 100% locked; line-break rag alone produces the second text, without moving graphic blocks across a poster.
Oulipopo
Detective fiction (1973)		 Fixed crime and physical evidence revealed in two clue sequences. "Let clue order guide suspicion while the same evidence determines the answer." vs. Ouhispo: Oulipopo never changes what happened in the past, only when the reader learns each clue; Ouhispo alters one historical fact and rewrites downstream records.
Ouhispo
History (1993)		 Counterfactual "Cleopatra's nose" pivot: freeze chronology prior to one altered event and update all subsequent documents. vs. Oulipopo: Mutates causal history forward from a single hinge point rather than reordering epistemic discovery of one fixed truth.
Oucipo
Cinema montage (c. 1974)		 Shot lengths locked to Fibonacci frame counts. "Give editorial attention a measurable price in frames. Reassign who gets the longest look by changing where a shot sits in the edit." vs. Exercices · Animated: Oucipo rations screen duration mathematically across cuts; Exercices · Animated keeps event timing constant and changes camera angle and staging.
Exercices de style · Animated
Animatics		 One locked animatic beat rendered through three distinct camera placements and staging rhythms. vs. Oucipo: Varies spatial framing and performance attitude over a fixed clock rather than redistributing frame budgets across shots.
Outrapo
Stage & theatre (1991)		 Stage blocking and cues written to play forward and backward. "Use the same score to make an arrival and an extraction. Give the reverse passage enough dramatic intent that an audience can follow what each performer wants." vs. Oucuipo: Reverses goal-directed physical action in time (entering becomes escaping), whereas Oucuipo mirrors sensory echoes across courses without reversing causality.
Oucuipo
Cooking (1990)		 Palindromic menu symmetric around a central course. "Let a technique recur with a different role in the meal. The last course should give the first a recognizable echo through texture or aroma." vs. Outrapo & Oumupo: Operates on irreversible appetite (a diner at course 5 remembers course 1), so symmetry turns repetition into a savory-to-sweet transformation.
Oumupo
Music (1960s)		 Phrase modules engineered with harmonic boundaries that survive any random or chosen shuffle. vs. Oucipo & Outrapo: Demands all-order invariance ($n!$ valid shuffles) rather than two mirrored passes or one Fibonacci duration ladder.
Oupeinpo
Painting (1980)		 Edge-compatible painted tiles permuted under a spectral color ban. "Make adjacency create a figure that the individual tiles cannot supply. Reassemble the same inventory so a continuous form becomes a dispersed field." vs. Ougrapo: Uses modular edge-continuity across equal tiles plus a forbidden hue; Ougrapo rebalances eye-tracking priority among five fixed graphic elements.
Ougrapo
Graphic design		 Exactly five geometric and typographic primitives rearranged into two opposite visual reading hierarchies. vs. Oupeinpo & Outypopo: Tests attentional entry order (what the eye hits first versus third) using scale and placement of five fixed shapes.
Oubapo
Comics (1992)		 Untouched panel art paired with two caption sequences. "Give the eye one stable image and the reader two changing contexts. A line at the center should acquire a different referent or intention according to which captions led to it." vs. Oucipo: Leaves image order untouched on the page while text sequencing alone flips what a drawn gesture means.
Ouphopo
Photography (1995)		 Shutter fired strictly at preset clock ticks along a mapped walk rather than by aesthetic framing. vs. Oucipo & Ouarchpo: Removes human selection at capture time so the clock samples whatever occupies the route, anti-decisive-moment style.
Ouarchpo
Architecture (2001)		 Floor plan whose doorways require a chess knight's L-step tour to enter every room once. vs. Ouphopo: Constrains topological adjacency (adjacent rooms cannot connect directly; movement jumps two over and one across).
Oupolpot
Civic procedure (2001)		 Identical voters and motions run under rotated speaking and voting agendas. vs. Oulipopo: Order changes collective decision power (Condorcet agenda effect) rather than reader suspicion about a past crime.

The 25 Proof Films: Historical Anchor, Real Build Status, and Perceptual Difference

Several films in the Screening Room look superficially alike until you name the exact variable each isolates. For example, La Machine à tuer le temps freezes a shot pool and reorders cuts over a shared sound bed, whereas La Cité Raymond Queneau freezes the picture edit completely and swaps two soundtracks. In Comics, Boucle-là ! flips an argument across a single spoken hinge line, Cercle vicieux reverses an entire multi-panel arc, Quatre-vingt-quinze reads one 2D matrix both across and down, and Les caïds de la gaudriole folds physical paper so separated ink edges meet.

Proof Film & Shelf Historical Original Cited Real Build & Verdict Perceptual Difference Tested (and Verbatim Thesis Where Sampled)
La Machine à tuer le temps
Cinema		 Oucipo & Queneau, c. 1974 unfilmed dossier of 42 stills (Drouot lot 175) 1:07 · 12 foraged
Not yet passed		 "Make the audience infer a different cause or motive from identical raw images." Differs from Cité Queneau by recutting shot order/duration rather than swapping soundtracks; failed blind review on rule legibility.
Un homme qui dort
Cinema		 Georges Perec & Bernard Queysanne, 1974 feature 1:12 · 8 foraged
Not yet passed		 "The proof hinges on one interval in which the voice's address and the image's point of view become perceptibly separate." Splits second-person "you" voiceover from an observed third-person body.
Les Lieux d'une fugue
Cinema		 Georges Perec, 1978 INA television film 0:57 · 6 foraged
Passed review		 Superimposes a remembered childhood runaway itinerary onto indifferent present-day street views; differs from Ellis Island by tracking one fugitive route rather than splitting archive and witness voices.
Récits d'Ellis Island
Cinema		 Robert Bober & Georges Perec, 1980 documentary 1:00 · 8 foraged
Passed review		 Separates three epistemic registers (ruined physical site, bureaucratic ledger, living spoken memory) so the viewer hears where record and remembrance diverge.
Le Chant du styrène
Cinema		 Alain Resnais & Raymond Queneau, 1958 industrial poem-film 0:38 · 4 foraged
Nearly passed		 "Hold a product long enough to make its shape familiar, then cut to the process or negative form that explains how it came into being." Reverses material causality in metered verse.
Zazie dans le métro
Cinema		 Louis Malle adapting Queneau, 1960 feature 0:22 · 10 foraged
Nearly passed		 Translates verbal wordplay directly into spatial slapstick, jump cuts, and street-level speed shifts rather than spoken dialogue jokes.
Renzo e Luciana
Cinema		 Mario Monicelli & Italo Calvino, 1962 episode of Boccaccio '70 1:12 · 17 foraged
Not yet passed		 Lets external shift clocks, workplace bans, and cramped apartment geometry choreograph when a couple can touch or speak.
Monsieur Ripois
Cinema		 René Clément, dialogue by Queneau, 1954 feature 0:45 · 10 foraged
Not yet passed		 Triangulates self-serving confession against visible camera fact and the listener's credulity inside a single sequence.
La Mort en ce jardin
Cinema		 Luis Buñuel, co-written by Queneau, 1956 feature 1:13 · 15 foraged
Passed review		 Introduces one anomalous surreal object into realist survival pressure so physical obstacle and dream logic redirect group choices.
Anémic cinéma
Cinema		 Marcel Duchamp, Man Ray & Marc Allégret, 1926 short 0:24 · 2 foraged
Passed review		 Alternates rotary optical depth illusion (Rotoreliefs) with spinning spiral alliterations that force the eye to switch between 3D space and reading.
Teuf-Teuf
Animation		 Jean Jabely, commentary by Queneau, 1956 animated short 0:44 · 6 foraged
Passed review		 "Each change in mechanism must visibly alter what a body, wheel, or material can do." Teaches mechanical evolution through visible kinematic consequence.
Bang Bang
Animation		 Jean Jabely & Queneau, c. 1958 storyboard dossier 0:30 · 6 foraged
Passed review		 Generates narrative friction between an impossible non-human witness and the visible storyboard apparatus staging the gag.
A Morning Stroll
Animation		 Grant Orchard / Studio AKA, 2011 short 1:08 · 12 foraged
Nearly passed		 Holds one sidewalk encounter invariant across three historical eras and rendering mediums; differs from Exercices by mutating world era and medium together.
Exercices de style
Variations		 Raymond Queneau, 1947 book (99 retellings of an S-bus incident) 1:10 · 9 foraged
Nearly passed		 "Show that form changes what someone notices in an ordinary event. Every variant should use a rule the reader can infer from what it does to the telling."
La Cité Raymond Queneau
Variations		 Olivier Azam & Laurent Firode, 1998 documentary 1:15 · 19 foraged
Not yet passed		 Locks one identical picture edit and plays it twice under two contrasting soundtracks so sound alone flips social meaning.
Exercises in Style · Mauro Martino
Variations		 Mauro Martino, 2023 AI exhibition piece 1:04 · 7 foraged
Nearly passed		 Isolates a single directional knob in a text-to-video instruction to measure what genuinely shifts versus what drifts on screen.
La Belle Hortense
Variations (Literature)		 Jacques Roubaud, 1985 Oulipian mystery novel 1:06 · 18 foraged
Not yet passed		 "Make a recurring motif gain detective value on its return." Uses six-element sestina spiral permutation to pace detective inference; currently fails blind critic legibility.
Le Maki Mococo
Variations		 Jean-Christophe Ribot after Jacques Roubaud 1:05 · 15 foraged
Nearly passed		 Externalizes reader reception in real time, showing how one arriving word, voice inflection, or image retroactively rewrites the prior shot.
Cercle vicieux
Comics		 Étienne Lécroart, 2000 Oubapo book 1:13 · pre-crew
Earlier version		 Long-form narrative palindrome: walks panel-by-panel to a midpoint, then traverses the exact panels in reverse so cause and effect invert.
Quatre-vingt-quinze
Comics		 Étienne Lécroart, Oubapo matrix comic 1:04 · 9 + page
Not yet passed		 2D orthogonal reading: the same drawn grid yields one coherent story read row-wise and a second story read column-wise.
Boucle-là !
Comics		 Étienne Lécroart, Oubapo single-page hinge 1:06 · 5 + page
Passed review		 "Build a tight conversational reversal in which the same speech and drawings change who seems to be on the defensive. The central line pivots the exchange within one page."
Moins d'un quart de seconde pour vivre
Comics		 Jean-Christophe Menu & Lewis Trondheim, 1991 1:06 · 2 + page
Passed review		 Zero visual change across repeated identical panels: proves dialogue pacing alone can drive action, suspense, and punchline.
Les caïds de la gaudriole
Comics		 Étienne Lécroart, Oubapo pliage strip 1:03 · 11 + page
Passed review		 "Make the fold itself change what the comic says. The open strip sets up a reading, then the same ink yields a surprising line or image when two edges meet."
99 Ways · Template
Comics		 Matt Madden, 99 Ways to Tell a Story (2005), p. 1 1:12 · 13 + page
Not yet passed		 Zero-style control group: stages an ordinary domestic beat with neutral clarity so 98 formal transformations have a shared yardstick.
99 Ways · Subjective
Comics		 Matt Madden, 99 Ways to Tell a Story (2005) 0:36 · pre-crew
Earlier version		 Restricts the camera strictly to one character's optical cone so the viewer infers action solely from partial first-person sightlines.
"The goal of potential literature is to furnish future writers with new techniques which can dismiss inspiration from their affectivity." (François Le Lionnais, August 28, 1961)
